core_obligations: The morphism of sites and the formulas (proof lines 4977-4982): the assumptions are those of the companion proposition, so the functor defines a morphism of sites, and the formulas for the pushforward and pullback follow from the cited results.
The composites (proof lines 4983-4986): the two composites of the pullback with the pushforward are isomorphic to the identity by the companion result on cocontinuous and fully faithful functors.

Full faithfulness of the pullback (proof lines 4989-5007): the map on morphism sets induced by the pullback is identified with the identity through adjunction and the composite identity, which proves the last assertion.
proof_roadmap: Apply the companion proposition and record the formulas for the two functors.
Use the companion result to compute the two composites.
Identify the morphism sets to prove full faithfulness of the pullback.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that when a functor between sites is cocontinuous, continuous, fully faithful and commutes with fibre products, and final objects correspond, then it defines a morphism of sites whose composition with the associated morphism of topoi is the identity and whose pullback is fully faithful (statement lines 4946-4974). The proof is a complete argument: the companion proposition gives the morphism of sites and the formulas for the two functors (proof lines 4977-4982); the companion result on cocontinuous and fully faithful functors gives that the two composites are isomorphic to the identity (proof lines 4983-4986); and full faithfulness of the pullback is proved by identifying the induced map on morphism sets with the identity through adjunction (proof lines 4989-5007). The non-formal content is the identification of the morphism sets. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
